scope: Meaning drafts in batches 06–15, 100 meanings and 300 authored questions

corrections.reason: The source says médiocrement affligé; removed a deeply distressed scenario and crying that overstated the degree.
La septième partie is one seventh of a whole, not the seventh position in a sequence.
The chapter I inadequate image and later faint voice need separate contextual review; retained only the former and aligned all questions with it.
Pieds and pouces de roi could both complete the previous blank; the revised five-foot geometric pace has a unique answer.
The old Son ___ blank made distractor honorifics grammatically wrong; revised sentence gives four compatible titles and contextual clues.

note: Checked source spans, intended contextual meanings and each three-band choice set for the next hundred drafts. Corrected five draft question/sense sets. Published exact-form candidates remain triage only, and final shared-identity mapping, the remaining batches and learner import are pending.

items.reviewNote: Source sense: Micromégas anatomically examines small creatures, not merely reading about or sketching them. The three question answers, in band order, are "dissected", "disséqua", "disséqua"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: With se and aux microscopes, the tiny organisms cannot be seen with ordinary microscopes; this is neither stealing nor deliberately hiding. The three question answers, in band order, are "escape notice", "dérobent", "dérobent"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Historical pejorative directed at the mufti for quibbling over insignificant matters; see CNRTL https://www.cnrtl.fr/definition/v%C3%A9tillard. The three question answers, in band order, are "petty and fault-finding", "vétillard", "vétillard"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The religious authority deems the propositions suspect; this is an accusation, not confirmation that they are false or criminal. The three question answers, in band order, are "suspicious", "suspectes", "suspectes"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: In the eighteenth-century theological formula propositions malsonnantes, an accusation that the words offend doctrine; not merely bad sounding or poorly written. Académie française 1762 https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A4M0210. The three question answers, in band order, are "offensive to doctrine", "malsonnantes", "malsonnantes"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Historical theological censure for propositions judged too daring and capable of implying false doctrine; Académie française 1762 https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A4T0225. The three question answers, in band order, are "rashly bold", "téméraires", "téméraires"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The mufti accuses the propositions of heresy; that label belongs to the accuser, not to the narrator’s endorsement. The three question answers, in band order, are "heretical", "hérétiques", "hérétiques"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The philosophical dispute absurdly concerns Sirius’s fleas; do not read as computer chips. The three question answers, in band order, are "fleas", "puces", "puces"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Snails compared with the imagined fleas of Sirius; zoological meaning, not a spiral staircase. The three question answers, in band order, are "snails", "colimaçons", "colimaçons"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The mufti has legal scholars condemn a book without reading it; do not conflate the book’s censure with sentencing its author. The three question answers, in band order, are "condemn", "condamner", "condamner"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: After studying insects, Micromégas wrote a book about them; not the unrelated arrangement of an object. The three question answers, in band order, are "wrote", "composa", "composa"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: « Un livre qui lui fit quelques affaires » means it brought trouble, specifically a prosecution, not commercial business or belongings. Académie française 1762: https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A4A0409. The three question answers, in band order, are "troubles", "affaires", "affaires"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The mufti actively pursued a case against the author for alleged heresy; not simply followed him in space. The three question answers, in band order, are "prosecuted", "poursuivit", "poursuivit"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The pronominal form describes Micromégas’s answer to the case; compare existing lem_zola_defendre / sns_fr_defendre_protect and sns_zola_defendre_protect before linking or separating the shared sense. The three question answers, in band order, are "defended himself", "défendit", "défendit"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: He was only slightly troubled by exile from a petty court; médiocrement modifies the degree of distress, not the fact of banishment. The three question answers, in band order, are "distressed", "affligé", "affligé"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The author must stay away from the court for eight hundred years, despite being only slightly distressed about it. The three question answers, in band order, are "banished", "banni", "banni"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The narrator contrasts human carriages with extraordinary celestial travel arrangements, not a ship’s crew. Historical vehicle and entourage senses: https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A3E0977. The three question answers, in band order, are "traveling conveyances", "équipages", "équipages"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The narrator says humans imagine only what fits their own familiar practices, not technical uses of an object. The three question answers, in band order, are "customs", "usages", "usages"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The court is full of trivial meanness, a criticism of character rather than of physical size. Académie française: https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A5P0941. The three question answers, in band order, are "pettiness", "petitesses", "petitesses"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Both microscopes and giant steps are compared to their familiar, normal versions. The published lemma lem_parure_ordinaire_adjective_35198f7a8a and sense sns_parure_ordinaire_commun_habituel_a8bfdb1e4d are likely reusable for a new plural surface after final review. The three question answers, in band order, are "usual", "ordinaires", "ordinaires"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: A planet around Sirius introduces the setting; the singular planète in later chapters needs a separate surface-form review. The three question answers, in band order, are "planets", "planètes", "planètes"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The planets move around Sirius, distinct from merely turning one’s body. Existing lem_parure_tourner_verb_b69185be96 / sns_parure_tourner_mouvoir_en_rond_par_un_mouvement_circulaire_ou_en_ligne_courbe_autour_d_un_axe_de_rotation_219c87f17f requires semantic comparison. The three question answers, in band order, are "orbit", "tournent", "tournent"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Sirius is the star’s name, not a person appointed to office. Existing lem_cendrillon_nommer_verb_bde5204dd3 / sns_cendrillon_nommer_attribuer_imposer_un_nom_a_une_personne_une_chose_ou_une_collectivite_6380ea9273 appears reusable after final identity review. The three question answers, in band order, are "called", "nommée", "nommée"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The narrator says he came to know Micromégas on a trip; compare existing lem_zola_connaitre / sns_zola_connaitre_know and sns_cendrillon_connaitre_faire_ou_avoir_fait_l_experience_permettant_une_representation_mentale_de_quelque_chose_ou_quelqu_un_avoir_l_idee_la_notion_d_une_personne_ou_d_une_chose_832d4989ec. The three question answers, in band order, are "get to know", "connaître", "connaître"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The narrator thinks the name suits a giant. Existing lem_convenir / sns_convenir_primary means agreeing on a decision, so this sense requires separation at signoff. The three question answers, in band order, are "suits", "convient", "convient"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: In « pas géométriques de cinq pieds chacun », the adjective identifies a historical fixed measure rather than casual walking steps. Académie française, 1798: https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A5P0383. The three question answers, in band order, are "fixed measuring paces", "géométriques", "géométriques"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: In « cinq pieds chacun », each individual measuring pace contains five feet; not all of them combined. The three question answers, in band order, are "each one", "chacun", "chacun"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Both uses concern geometers reaching a numerical conclusion. Existing trouver senses for discovering, judging and finding oneself require explicit comparison; no automatic reuse. The three question answers, in band order, are "will calculate", "trouveront", "trouveront"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The planet is the giant’s place of origin, figuratively described as having produced him. Existing lem_zola_produire / sns_zola_produire_present concerns presenting evidence, not this sense. The three question answers, in band order, are "gave rise to", "produit", "produit"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: All four uses quantify lengths, circumference or people; historical units remain as printed but the numerical magnitude is unchanged. The three question answers, in band order, are "millions", "millions", "millions"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The narrator’s most recent journey, not the second of two items; compare the published Zola sense before reuse. The three question answers, in band order, are "most recent", "dernier", "dernier"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The name Micromégas follows se; do not confuse this pronominal naming use with calling aloud. The three question answers, in band order, are "was called", "appelait", "appelait"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The narrator ironically calls geometers useful to society; the adjective’s lexical sense remains useful. The three question answers, in band order, are "useful", "utiles", "utiles"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Au public denotes the community benefiting from geometers, not the published adjective sense accessible to everyone. The three question answers, in band order, are "people in general", "public", "public"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The geometers will take up a pen to calculate, a literal action with a familiar metonym for writing. The three question answers, in band order, are "will pick up", "prendront", "prendront"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Prendre la plume refers to writing, not a bird’s feather used in isolation; compare any published senses before shared reuse. The three question answers, in band order, are "writing pen", "plume", "plume"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The narrator’s parenthetical dis-je marks his own interruption; distinguish from second-person dis in other contexts. The three question answers, in band order, are "I say", "dis", "dis"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Il faut absolument emphasizes necessity in the satirical calculation, not an approval of its truth. The three question answers, in band order, are "it is essential", "absolument", "absolument"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Rien n’est plus simple is the narrator’s ironic claim that the calculation is obvious; compare published simple sense. The three question answers, in band order, are "easy to understand", "simple", "simple"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Rien n’est plus ordinaire is ironic but uses the usual/common sense; compare the published La Parure sense. The three question answers, in band order, are "common", "ordinaire", "ordinaire"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The small German and Italian rulers’ States are political territories, distinct from conditions or physical states; the capital É belongs to the printed proper political designation, not a separate lexical sense. The three question answers, in band order, are "political territories", "États", "États"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Political rulers of small German or Italian states, not an adjective meaning independent. The three question answers, in band order, are "rulers", "souverains", "souverains"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The small states are measured against a vast empire to show scale, not judged equally valuable. The three question answers, in band order, are "compared", "comparés", "comparés"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The Turkish, Muscovite and Chinese territories provide the contrast in size with minor European rulers’ states; this is a political realm. The three question answers, in band order, are "empire", "empire", "empire"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: A weak image is an imperfect illustration of the immense differences in nature, not a literal photograph. The three question answers, in band order, are "illustration", "image", "image"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Describes the vast differences among beings, rather than a supernatural claim. The feminine plural agrees with différences. The three question answers, in band order, are "astonishingly great", "prodigieuses", "prodigieuses"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The giant’s ceinture is a belt measured around his body in the geometrical joke; no implied planetary belt. The three question answers, in band order, are "belt", "ceinture", "ceinture"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: In la septième partie de la hauteur, the face measures one of seven equal portions of the body height; this describes a fraction of a whole, not a position in a sequence. The three question answers, in band order, are "one seventh of the whole", "septième", "septième"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Ce qui était à démontrer closes an ironically elaborate geometrical proof; it does not mean merely to display an object. The three question answers, in band order, are "prove", "démontrer", "démontrer"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Étudier au collège at that age follows the Sirius society’s established custom, not a personal promise or a written law. The three question answers, in band order, are "custom", "coutume", "coutume"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: All four workwide uses measure or describe bodily stature. The published waist sense is inapplicable to the giant’s height and the small woman’s stature. The three question answers, in band order, are "height", "taille", "taille"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: All five workwide uses mean an anatomical or physical body, including the body contrasted with the soul. The published institutional corps sense is wrong here. The three question answers, in band order, are "body", "corps", "corps"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The source refers to Blaise Pascal’s sister in the singular. The published exact-form gloss incorrectly says sisters. The three question answers, in band order, are "sister", "sœur", "sœur"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Chaise de poste names a historical travel carriage, paired with berline; it is not the published household chair sense. The three question answers, in band order, are "travel carriage", "chaise", "chaise"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The censor pursued the writer forcefully, not necessarily quickly. The published quickly/eagerly gloss is misleading in this prosecution context. The three question answers, in band order, are "vigorously", "vivement", "vivement"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The three chapter I measures and one later negative participial clause describe an existing state or circumstance, not a new event. The three question answers, in band order, are "being", "étant", "étant"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Both de branche en branche uses are a bird’s movement among actual limbs of a tree, not a figurative field of study. The three question answers, in band order, are "tree branch", "branche", "branche"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Both chapter I uses describe the giant’s anatomical nose measured against his face and body. The three question answers, in band order, are "nose", "nez", "nez"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The travelers and the secretary are surprised by unexpected things; both occurrences describe a reaction to novelty. The three question answers, in band order, are "surprised", "étonnés", "étonnés"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The young Sirian studies at the most famous collège on his planet, an educational institution, not a professional association. The three question answers, in band order, are "school", "collège", "collège"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Both chapter I occurrences multiply twenty-four by a thousand in the giant’s measure. The hyphenated numeral is a single orthographic token. The three question answers, in band order, are "twenty-four", "vingt-quatre", "vingt-quatre"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The chapter’s neuf mille and neuf cents and the later neuf cents are the numeral nine, not the adjective meaning new; compound trente-neuf and dix-neuf are separate printed tokens. The three question answers, in band order, are "nine", "neuf", "neuf"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Tantôt ... tantôt contrasts riding a ray of sunlight with traveling by comet; not a future adverb meaning soon. The three question answers, in band order, are "at one moment; then", "tantôt", "tantôt"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The source contrasts beings in nature and observes differences alongside proportions; both uses are plural noun distinctions. The three question answers, in band order, are "differences", "différences", "différences"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Pascal becomes a mediocre geometer and the later small human accurately measures a Saturnian. Both are people practicing geometry, not the instrument. The three question answers, in band order, are "geometer", "géomètre", "géomètre"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The chapter I image inadequately represents the differences in nature. The later faint voice is a separate acoustic context left for review before it is assigned a shared sense. The three question answers, in band order, are "inadequate as a representation", "faible", "faible"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The small territories can be circled in a half-hour; the hyphenated time noun is one orthographic token. The three question answers, in band order, are "thirty minutes", "demi-heure", "demi-heure"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The sculptors and painters will agree that the giant’s belt has the calculated circumference; it is not the suitable/fitting sense of convenir. The three question answers, in band order, are "will agree", "conviendront", "conviendront"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: At about age 450 in the comic scale of Sirius he has just left childhood; this means the early stage of life. The three question answers, in band order, are "childhood", "enfance", "enfance"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The Saturnians are called nains only relative to the much larger Sirian, even though they are a thousand toises tall. The satirical scale is essential to the meaning. The three question answers, in band order, are "very small people by comparison", "nains", "nains"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Fourteen of eighteen workwide uses give length, height, diameter or circumference. Four other uses describe anatomical feet, including one already assigned a published body-part identity in chapter I. Pieds de roi is a historical length measure. The three question answers, in band order, are "feet as length units", "pieds", "pieds"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Three chapter I de haut uses give vertical size. The later tout haut means aloud, while de haut en bas means from top to bottom and is held for a separate published identity. The three question answers, in band order, are "tall", "haut", "haut"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The Earth, the belt and a ball are measured de tour: the whole distance around their perimeter, not an occasion or a stroll. The three question answers, in band order, are "circumference", "tour", "tour"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Faire le tour of a country or the globe is to travel once around it. The separate circumference sense measures that route without undertaking the journey. The three question answers, in band order, are "complete circuit", "tour", "tour"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Seven workwide fois plus or fois moins contexts multiply a measure; other fois uses mean an occasion and stay with the published occasion sense. The chapter I occurrences are both numerical comparisons. The three question answers, in band order, are "times as many", "fois", "fois"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Vingt-quatre mille paces of five feet each amount to one hundred twenty thousand feet. Later font expresses causation or pronominal action; this is a selected contextual sense subset. The three question answers, in band order, are "amount to", "font", "font"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Forme substantielle names a disputed scholastic principle thought to determine the nature of fleas. The existing surface’s outward shape sense is unsuitable; five later forme uses concern outward shape or changed bodily form. The three question answers, in band order, are "supposed inner nature in scholastic philosophy", "forme", "forme"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The narrator specifies twenty-one million times six hundred thousand in his exaggerated comparison; the hyphenated numeral is one token. The three question answers, in band order, are "twenty-one", "vingt-un", "vingt-un"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Part of the nose-length arithmetic: three hundred thirty-three feet, a single hyphenated number token. The three question answers, in band order, are "thirty-three", "trente-trois", "trente-trois"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Pascal divines thirty-two propositions and a later astronomical answer gives thirty-two and a half degrees. Both are the same hyphenated numeral. The three question answers, in band order, are "thirty-two", "trente-deux", "trente-deux"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Nature has placed differences among all beings. The participle agrees with the preceding object différences; this is an actual placement metaphor, not se mettre à beginning an activity. The three question answers, in band order, are "placed", "mises", "mises"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Son Excellence is an honorific for Micromégas in all three uses, including the later chapters. The source’s capital E signals a title, not abstract excellence as a quality. The three question answers, in band order, are "Excellency as a title", "Excellence", "Excellence"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Que j’ai dite refers back to the height the narrator has already stated. Feminine agreement follows the preceding object hauteur. The three question answers, in band order, are "mentioned", "dite", "dite"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The narrator calls the numerical proportion très-jolie, an evaluative and possibly playful compliment to his elaborate geometrical argument; the hyphen belongs to the selected orthography. The three question answers, in band order, are "very pretty", "très-jolie", "très-jolie"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The giant’s face, nose and body are compared by ratios; the later en proportion describes the same relation between corresponding organs. The three question answers, in band order, are "ratio between parts", "proportion", "proportion"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Des plus cultivés describes learned and intellectually developed minds, not agricultural land. The three question answers, in band order, are "highly educated", "cultivés", "cultivés"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: L’un des plus cultivés que nous ayons uses subjunctive avoir after the superlative; it denotes belonging to the narrator’s known group, not a different lexical action. The three question answers, in band order, are "that we have", "ayons", "ayons"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: He has invented some of the things he knows; feminine plural quelques-unes refers back to choses, not all of them or one alone. The three question answers, in band order, are "some of them", "quelques-unes", "quelques-unes"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The Sirian was a pupil studying at the most famous school on his planet; this imperfect describes an ongoing past activity. The three question answers, in band order, are "was studying", "étudiait", "étudiait"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Selon la coutume and selon Homère introduce the convention or the named source on which the statement relies. The three question answers, in band order, are "according to", "selon", "selon"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The Sirian attends the most renowned school on his planet, not a festival or a public celebration. The three question answers, in band order, are "most famous", "célèbre", "célèbre"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: He figured out more than fifty geometrical propositions by his intelligence, without an explicit proof in the narrative. The three question answers, in band order, are "figured out", "devina", "devina"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Pascal intuited thirty-two propositions and another thinker correctly inferred Earth’s flattened shape. Both cases mean reaching a conclusion by insight. The three question answers, in band order, are "figured out", "deviné", "deviné"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: En se jouant presents Pascal’s solving the propositions with playful ease, not a literal game. It is a historical idiom in the cited remark about his mathematics. The three question answers, in band order, are "with playful ease", "jouant", "jouant"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Pascal became a geometer, and later the conversation became interesting; both are changes of state, not mere movement. The three question answers, in band order, are "became", "devint", "devint"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Livre fort curieux describes a striking or intriguing book. The later two curieux are curious people as nouns and remain unassigned to a separate learner identity. The three question answers, in band order, are "intriguing", "curieux", "curieux"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The censor is described as ignorant despite his confident judgment; this concerns lack of knowledge, not a deliberate refusal to acknowledge someone. The three question answers, in band order, are "lacking knowledge", "ignorant", "ignorant"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Forme substantielle is the scholastic term under dispute, not a claim that the flea has a large or materially substantial shape. The three question answers, in band order, are "pertaining to an inner philosophical essence", "substantielle", "substantielle"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The chapter I narrator contrasts vehicles up there with ours, and a later speaker locates the philosopher above the Earth. The hyphenated expression is a single token. The three question answers, in band order, are "up there", "là-haut", "là-haut"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Micromégas crossed the Milky Way in little time, a movement through a region rather than a static observation. The three question answers, in band order, are "traversed", "parcourut", "parcourut"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.
